anomalies.observed: The isolated CAN transceivers U49 and U55 have both their logic-side ground (GND1) and bus-side ground (GND2) connected to the same GND net.
anomalies.expected: For isolated CAN transceivers, GND1 and GND2 must be on separate isolated grounds to maintain galvanic isolation, as required by the specification's 'two isolated CAN buses'.
anomalies.impact: The isolation barrier is shorted, defeating the purpose of the isolated transceivers. This creates a common ground between the CM4 and the CAN bus, which can cause ground loops, noise, and safety issues.

anomalies.observed: The anodes of LEDs D24, D29, and D42 are all tied together on net /NET0072, which has no connection to any power supply or other net.
anomalies.expected: LED anodes should be connected to a positive supply (e.g., +3V3) so that current can flow through the LEDs when their cathodes are pulled low.
anomalies.impact: These LEDs will never light because they have no power source, so the intended status indication is missing.

anomalies.observed: R61 is a 10k resistor connected between /NET0138 and GND, acting as a pull-down. /NET0138 also connects to U33.4 (open-drain output of SN74LVC1G07), Q1.1 (gate of N-MOSFET), and U36.5 (OE of level shifter). Since U33 is open-drain and can only pull low, /NET0138 is always low.
anomalies.expected: /NET0138 should be pulled up to +3V3 (e.g., R61 connected to +3V3) so that when U33 is off, the net is high, turning on Q1 and enabling U36. Other similar e-stop sink control nets (e.g., /NET0143, /NET0150) are pulled up to +3V3.
anomalies.impact: Q1 never turns on, so the WS2812B LEDs (D1, D6, D8, D16, D25, D32, D47) have no ground and cannot light. U36 is disabled, so the level-shifted data to the WS2812B LEDs is blocked. This disables the addressable status LEDs described in the specification.

parsed.summary: The design files contain multiple anomalies: the isolated CAN transceivers have their grounds shorted, three status LEDs have floating anodes, and a pull-down on the WS2812B enable net prevents the addressable LEDs from working.
